s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive dyspnea on exertion with electrocardiographic changes and cardiac mass
salient_findings: ST elevation in leads V1, V2, and V3
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
History of multiple prior cardiac events
History of lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium
Received 2 drug-eluting stents to the right coronary artery 10 months prior
High-sensitivity cardiac troponin-T level was 40 ng/L
ECG showed normal sinus rhythm at 90 beats per minute
ECG showed T-wave inversions in leads I, aVL, V4, V5, and V6
Transthoracic echocardiogram showed preserved left ventricular systolic function
Large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade
Coronary angiography showed nonobstructive epicardial coronary artery disease

shortlist.label: Cardiac Metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: History of lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium, and presence of a cardiac mass

shortlist.label: Myocardial Infarction with Cardiac Rupture
shortlist.why_kept: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin-T level was elevated, and ECG showed ST elevation and T-wave inversions

shortlist.label: Pericardial Metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: Large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade, and history of lung cancer

shortlist.label: Cardiac Sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a cardiac mass, although less likely given the patient's history of lung cancer

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma of the heart
shortlist.why_kept: Although rare, it is a possible cause of a cardiac mass, and the patient's age and sex are consistent with this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium, and the echocardiogram shows a well-circumscribed mass in the left ventricle, which is consistent with cardiac metastasis.

rejected.label: Myocardial Infarction with Cardiac Rupture
rejected.why: The coronary angiography shows nonobstructive epicardial coronary artery disease, and the echocardiogram does not show regional wall motion abnormalities, making myocardial infarction with cardiac rupture less likely.

rejected.label: Pericardial Metastasis
rejected.why: While pericardial effusion is present, the primary finding is the intracardiac mass, which suggests cardiac metastasis rather than pericardial metastasis.

rejected.label: Cardiac Sarcoma
rejected.why: There is no indication of a primary cardiac tumor, and the patient's history of lung cancer with metastatic disease makes cardiac metastasis a more likely explanation for the intracardiac mass.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma of the heart
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence to suggest a primary cardiac angiosarcoma, and the patient's history and imaging findings are more consistent with cardiac metastasis from lung cancer.
